notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already used up (no search ran), so everything was read by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, robots.txt read first for each host: the campaign websites as filed with the Secretary of State (learned from a scratch copy of the database on which python -m ballot.local_sites files had been run), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, and the University of Minnesota's election archive. No campaign site was found beyond those filed.

Filed websites not recorded: Aaron Schweiger's (www.aaronformn.com answers, but shows a script and the page reader only the word "Aaron": no office or place) and Alexander Koenig's (brooklyncenter2030.org shows a registrar's "Coming Soon" holding page).

No birth year is recorded. The election archive shows birth dates for Kenneth Smoron and Aaron Schweiger, but the source it names is a birth records index, so they were not taken (as in other parts). Luis Withrow's site gives an age without a date.

The election archive is labelled secondary, as in other parts. Alexander Koenig's 2018 run rests on name, state and city (the archive ties its Koenig to Brooklyn Center); it does not mention 2026. Worth the second reader's eye.

Garrison McMurtrey's campaign site says "DFL & Labor Endorsed" (his own words); no DFL page naming him for 2026 was found (dfl.org's list does not; saintpauldfl.org speaks only of a coming school board convention), so no endorsed_by. The same for Luis Withrow ("Republican Endorsed Candidate"): mngop.com names no legislative candidates and no local unit's page was reached. Omar Syed's endorsements page names officeholders, not a party unit endorsing him. Chair of the Saint Paul DFL (McMurtrey) is a party post, not an office, and was left out; family details on campaign and county pages were not taken.

Not sitting in the office sought, by the government's own pages: Heidi Wersal (Redwood County lists Jim Salfer for District 2), Alexander Koenig, Joe Tougas, Christian Grams, Eric DeGroot and Miranda Lape (not on their cities' council pages), Erin Stoneking (not on Albert Lea's board page).

Not reached, nothing worked around: Red Lake County's site (its certificate is not valid for the address), Pope County's site (an empty shell to a script), Columbia Heights (robots.txt asks scripts to stay out), the Minnesota Judicial Branch (robots.txt, so nothing for Judge Steven Bradley Hanke), the Dassel-Cokato and Sartell-St. Stephen school sites (no answer), Lake Superior School District (a redirect that never lands). Bjorn Olson filed no website and none was found by trying addresses.

Nothing citable for thirteen: Bjorn Olson, Casey J. Klipping, Heidi Wersal, Nathan Brecht, Joe Tougas, Judah Scharnhorst, Christian Grams, Eric DeGroot, Erin Stoneking, Clint Scherping, Nate Crowe, Jeff Radle, Steven Bradley Hanke.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: all 23 cited pages were opened again with the kit's honest User-Agent and every one answered; all 33 findings stand. Each filed website was found in the Secretary of State's filing files beside the candidate's name. Two wordings corrected (Miranda Lape's site: the ward is in the page's data, and the date it prints is November 4th; the DFL list prints no year). The election archive's note on Aaron Schweiger spells the name "Schweigert" once; its heading, its 2004 rows (primary won, general lost) and the 2026 District 3B run from Duluth fit. Alexander Koenig's 2018 run is kept on two anchors (Minnesota, Brooklyn Center, where the archive says he lived and ran for council in 2016); the archive does not mention 2026.
